title: HBV structure, genes and natural history
guide: Hepadnavirus, relaxed circular partially dsDNA, (+) incomplete primer / (−) complete RT; 42 nm Dane, 10 genotypes, 4 ORFs; S→HBsAg, C→HBcAg (intracellular), pre-C→HBeAg qualitative, P→polymerase/RT, X→HBxAg HCC; 60-day IP, 95–99% recovery, 1–5% chronic (95% vertical), cirrhosis → PHTN/HCC/liver failure, NASH also, no treatment; 100× HIV, 10× HCV; HAV 1, HEV 4 genotypes, A commonest, C HCC; all fluids except stool; 90/10 rule by HBeAg.

title: Acute hepatitis B: transmission, symptoms, markers and interpretation
guide: Vertical, percutaneous 6–30% (HCV 0.6–6.1%), sexual not established, transfusion 1:200,000 & 1:1,800,000 HBV>HCV; no feco-oral/breast milk; post-transfusion CMV>EBV>HCV; 2–3 day prodrome after 60 days; anti-HAV IgM children, anti-HEV IgM adults → HBsAg/HBeAg/anti-HBc IgM; marker curve colours and 24–32 wk window; HBeAg + vs − interpretation, pre-core mutant; S/escape/occult mutants lose HBsAg, best test anti-HBc IgM; basal core mutant 30% HBeAg; HBV DNA best acute marker.

title: Progression, follow-up, chronic profile and serological patterns
guide: Recovery 95–99%, chronic 1–5%, AFH 0.1–1% vs 5–20% with HDV; follow-up 24 wk/12–16 wk; conversions to anti-HBs, anti-HBc IgM (as printed), anti-HBe = recovery; HBsAg + anti-HBc IgG = chronic; HBeAg + → DNA >20,000; HBeAg − → >2,000 high vs <2,000 carriers (no Rx, HCC risk); pre-core/basal core mutant poor prognosis; 8-row serological pattern table including window, reactivation, remote/escape, recovery, immunisation.
